claims.text: NOAA (4 August 2026), on its GOES-West satellite smoke-monitoring coverage of the Pacific Northwest fires: "Hundreds of thousands of acres of land have been scorched so far by dozens of wildfires across the Pacific Northwest region, and many remain minimally contained. The fires have degraded air quality and caused evacuations of tens of thousands of people across Washington and Idaho."

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Washington State
claims.text: Washington Governor Ferguson's statewide wildfire emergency proclamation (1 August 2026) states 'over 1,000 fires have burned approximately 425,000 acres statewide -- the highest acreage since 2021,' with 200,000+ acres actively burning across 12 large fires; a federal emergency declaration approved 4 August 2026 covers Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens and Yakima counties plus the Yakama Nation, Colville Reservation and Spokane Tribe of Indians, with 110 Washington National Guard members activated and 13 State Fire Marshal task forces mobilized.

InciWeb Sinlahekin Fire incident page, updated 16 August 2026, 10:41 p.m. PT: the fire holds at 152,682 acres (unchanged from 15 August) with containment up to 44% (from 42%) and 1,736 personnel assigned (up from 1,677), estimated full-containment date still 19 August 2026; InciWeb notes 'light, lingering heat remains in select areas of the incident where heavy dead and down fuels continue to burn.'

InciWeb Sinlahekin Fire incident page, updated 17 August 2026, 10:45 p.m. PT: the fire has grown to 153,843 acres (up from 152,682 acres on 16 August) with containment holding at 44% and 1,731 personnel assigned (down from 1,736), estimated full-containment date still 19 August 2026; the page continues to note light, lingering heat in select areas where heavy dead-and-down fuels continue to burn.

InciWeb Sinlahekin Fire incident page, updated 18 August 2026: the fire has grown to 154,162 acres (up from 153,843 acres on 17 August) with containment holding at 44% and 1,645 personnel assigned (down from 1,731); a wetting rain overnight reduced fire activity in the central portion of the fire, though the northern and southern portions remained drier with continued fire activity, and crews continued strengthening containment lines near Salmon Meadows and Toats Coulee while continuing structure defense in the Toby's Mill area. Level 2 'be set to evacuate' evacuations remain in place for the Toby's Mill area, and recreation areas between Conconully and Loomis remain closed.

InciWeb Sinlahekin Fire incident page, current as of 19 August 2026, 9:18 p.m. PT: the fire has grown to 154,250 acres (up from 154,162 acres on 18 August) with containment holding at 44% and 1,731 personnel assigned (up from 1,645).

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Washington State
claims.text: Office of the Governor of Washington State (4 August 2026): announces that President Trump approved a federal emergency declaration for Washington's wildfires, covering Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens and Yakima counties and the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation, the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, and the Spokane Tribe of Indians; Governor Ferguson: "The declaration allows our federal partners to mobilize their resources and personnel to support our response, and unlocks resources for state, local and tribal governments," including support for "evacuating and providing emergency shelters for people who are displaced by the wildfires," "emergency food and water, search and rescue operations and more." This followed Governor Ferguson's own statewide wildfire emergency proclamation of 1 August 2026. No casualty, structure-loss, or acreage figures are given in this release.

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Washington State
claims.text: On 7 August 2026 the US Department of Health and Human Services approved Governor Ferguson's request to declare a federal Public Health Emergency in response to the Eastern Washington wildfires, covering the same six counties (Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Yakima) and three tribal nations (Yakama Nation, Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, Spokane Tribe of Indians) already covered by the 4 August 2026 federal emergency declaration.

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Washington State
claims.text: On 7 August 2026, Governor Bob Ferguson's office announced that the US Department of Health and Human Services approved his request to declare a Public Health Emergency for the wildfire-affected areas of Eastern Washington -- Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens and Yakima counties, plus the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation, the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, and the Spokane Tribe of Indians. This is a second, stacked federal declaration alongside the major disaster/emergency declaration Washington received on 4 August 2026. No death or displacement figures have been published on an allowlisted source.

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Washington State
claims.text: On 10 August 2026, Governor Bob Ferguson signed an emergency proclamation suspending numerous state laws to help those affected by the wildfires, now covering Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Douglas and Yakima counties plus the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation, the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, and the Spokane Tribe of Indians (adding Douglas County to the area covered by the 4 August federal emergency declaration). The Governor's office states: "My emergency proclamation waives and suspends numerous state laws so that help can move quickly," and the proclamation suspends disaster cash assistance eligibility requirements, personal document replacement fees, professional license renewal deadlines, unemployment benefit waiting periods and job-search requirements, a two-week limitation on eviction-related actions, healthcare provider licensing and supervision requirements, hospital and pharmacy licensing restrictions, and adult family home/assisted living facility capacity limitations, and waives late fees for employers unable to file or pay second-quarter 2026 taxes because of the wildfires. No death toll, injury count, acreage, containment, or displacement figures are given in this release.

InciWeb (the US federal wildland fire agencies' official incident-information system), Sinlahekin Fire incident page, updated Tuesday 11 August 2026, 10:46 p.m. PT: the Sinlahekin Fire -- now the state's largest -- stands at 150,241 acres and 42% contained, with 1,541 personnel assigned and an estimated containment date of 19 August 2026; current guidance for nearby residents is to 'Stay ready to evacuate if conditions change.'

InciWeb Sinlahekin Fire incident page, updated 12 August 2026 21:34 PT: the fire stands at 152,921 acres and 37% contained (up from 150,241 acres / 42% contained on 11 August), with 1,593 personnel assigned (up from 1,541) and an estimated containment date of 19 August 2026; evacuation guidance remains 'Stay ready to evacuate if conditions change.'

InciWeb Sinlahekin Fire incident page, updated Thursday 13 August 2026, 9:26 p.m. PT: acreage 151,850 acres, containment 42% (up from 37% on 12 August; acreage essentially unchanged from 152,921), 1,600 personnel assigned (up from 1,593), estimated containment date 19 August 2026.

InciWeb (update posted 15 August 2026, 10:31 PM): the Sinlahekin Fire has grown to 152,682 acres and is 42% contained (1,677 personnel assigned), with an estimated full-containment date of 19 August 2026; the fire started 26 July 2026 from a lightning strike about 12 miles west of Tonasket, WA.

description: Dozens of wildfires broke out across the Pacific Northwest in late July and early August 2026, burning hundreds of thousands of acres and forcing evacuations of tens of thousands of people across eastern Washington State and into Idaho. Governor Bob Ferguson proclaimed a statewide wildfire emergency on 1 August, and a federal emergency declaration approved on 4 August 2026 covers Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens and Yakima counties plus the Yakama Nation, the Colville Reservation and the Spokane Tribe of Indians; the governor's office reports over 1,000 fires and approximately 425,000 acres burned statewide, the highest acreage since 2021, with 110 National Guard members activated. The Sinlahekin Fire, the state's largest, had grown to 154,250 acres and was 44% contained on 19 August 2026, with 1,731 personnel assigned. No confirmed death toll or structure-loss count has been published for the emergency as a whole.

impact.summary: The Sinlahekin Fire, the state's largest, started by a lightning strike on 26 July 2026 about 12 miles west of Tonasket and had grown to 154,250 acres at 44% containment on 19 August 2026, with 1,731 personnel assigned and Level 2 evacuation notices still in place for the Toby's Mill area. Statewide, the governor's office reports over 1,000 fires and approximately 425,000 acres burned, the highest acreage since 2021, with 200,000+ acres actively burning across 12 large fires at the emergency's height, 110 National Guard members activated and 13 State Fire Marshal task forces mobilized. Federal emergency and Public Health Emergency declarations cover six counties and three tribal nations; no confirmed death toll or structure-loss figure has been published.
